title: Release and verify
summary: A collection of nouns and verbs for releasing a change and proving what is live: a plan around the exact tested head, checks confirmed on that head, the release owner's act recorded with its identifiers, live bytes compared with built bytes, read-only smoke checks, a kept rollback target and one receipt whose verdict follows from its parts.
boundaries: Workers plan, read, hash, check and record. Landing changes, switching live versions and changing host settings are the release owner's acts, recorded by a person's verb.
Every network request in these verbs is read-only; a check that would write runs only against a target the release owner named for it.
A failed or partial receipt stays on the record; the next attempt gets its own receipt.
Workers create nouns and propose verbs; an authorized requester enqueues the proposals worth doing.
Importing the pack writes nothing and enqueues nothing.

nouns.title: How a release is planned, checked, recorded and verified
nouns.category_reason: A reusable procedure with guardrails, followed by every verb in this pack.

lifecycle: plan-release names the tested head, required checks, holds, rollback target, parity method, smoke checks and the owner's acts.
check-head confirms every required check ran and passed on that exact head.
The release owner lands the change and switches the live version, then records both with record-release.
verify-parity hashes the live bytes and compares them with the built bytes.
run-smoke checks live behavior with read-only requests.
write-receipt assembles the chain and derives the verdict from its parts.
prepare-rollback briefs the release owner when parity or a smoke check fails.
rules: If the landed commit differs from the tested head, the checks run again on the landed commit before anything goes live.
A release without a recorded rollback target is incomplete.
Partial evidence gives a partial verdict that lists exactly what was not checked.

Workers create nouns and propose verbs; they never enqueue.

nouns.title: Who may do what in a release
nouns.category_reason: A deterministic rule that separates worker verbs from the release owner's acts.

switching or reverting a live version
changing names, addresses or settings on a host

value.never: A worker never performs a release owner act, even when its credentials would allow it.

verbs.title: Plan the release
verbs.summary: Write a release plan around the exact tested head: required checks, holds, rollback target, parity method, smoke checks and the acts only the release owner performs.
verbs.outcome: A release plan the release owner can follow step by step.

slots.name: change
slots.description: Pin of the change to release, naming the exact commit that was tested.

steps: Take the tested head from the pinned change and name the checks the repository requires for it.
Record holds and freezes that apply; a hold stops the plan here.
Record the current live version as the rollback target.
Choose the parity method for the target type and the smoke checks for what the change touched.
List the acts only the release owner performs, in order. Never perform any of them yourself.

acceptance.check: The plan validates against template.release-plan's schema.
tested_head equals the pinned change's tested commit.
No owner act appears as a worker step.

verbs.title: Confirm the checks on the exact head
verbs.summary: Read the check runs for the exact head and confirm every required check ran and passed on it.
verbs.outcome: A head check: ready, not_ready or unknown.
steps: Read every run for the plan's tested head from the code host.
Count a required check as missing if its latest run is on any other head, or did not succeed.
Mark ready only when nothing required is missing; never rerun or change anything.

acceptance.check: The head check validates against template.head-check's schema.
Every run counted as passing has head equal to the plan's tested head.
verdict ready exactly when missing_required is empty.

network: Read-only requests to the code host's check-run API for the named repository; nothing is changed.
capabilities: read-only access to the repository's check runs
write candidate nouns in the requester's scope

verbs.title: Record what the release owner carried out
verbs.summary: The release owner records the commit they landed, the version now live and the version it replaced. This template performs nothing itself.
verbs.outcome: A release record with the landed commit, the live version and the rollback target.

slots.name: head_check
slots.description: Pin of the head check that said ready.

steps: Write the identifiers exactly as the code host and the host report them.
If the landed commit differs from the tested head, say so in notes and have the checks rerun on it.

acceptance.check: The record validates against template.release-record's schema.
previous_version is filled whenever deployed_version is.

verbs.title: Compare live bytes with built bytes
verbs.summary: Hash what is live for the recorded version and compare it with the digests of the build.
verbs.outcome: A parity check: match, mismatch or unknown with the reason.

slots.name: build
slots.description: Pin of the build with its file digests.

steps: Use the parity method for the target type, bypassing caches where the host allows it.
Compare every expected digest; list each mismatch by path.
Write unknown with the reason whenever the live bytes cannot be read; never write match from partial evidence.

acceptance.check: The parity check validates against template.parity-check's schema.
verdict match only when every expected path was observed with an equal digest.
verdict unknown only with why_unknown filled.

network: Read-only requests to the live target's public addresses for the files being compared; nothing is changed.

verbs.title: Run read-only smoke checks
verbs.summary: Run the planned smoke checks against the live version with read-only requests and record each result with evidence.
verbs.outcome: A smoke report with every check passed, failed or not run.

slots.name: release_plan
slots.description: Pin of the release plan listing the smoke checks.

slots.name: release_record
slots.description: Pin of the release record naming the live version.

steps: Run each planned check with read-only requests and keep the response evidence short.
Skip any check that would write unless the release owner named a target for it; record it as not_run with the reason.
Count failed checks exactly; never retry a failure into a pass without recording both runs.

acceptance.check: The smoke report validates against template.smoke-report's schema.
failed equals the number of checks with result fail.
Every not_run check has a reason.

network: Read-only requests to the live target's public addresses named in the plan; nothing is changed.

verbs.title: Write the release receipt
verbs.summary: Assemble the plan, head check, release record, parity check and smoke report into one receipt whose verdict follows from its parts.
verbs.outcome: A release receipt that passes the release checks.

slots.name: parts
slots.description: Pins of the head check, release record, parity check and smoke report.

steps: Copy identifiers from the parts exactly; never fill a gap from memory.
Derive the verdict from the parts: verified, partially_verified with not_checked, failed or unknown.
Run the release checks on the receipt before writing it; propose prepare-rollback when parity or a smoke check failed.

acceptance.check: The receipt validates against template.release-receipt's schema.
The receipt passes the pinned release checks.
Recomputing the verdict from the pinned parts gives the same verdict.

verbs.title: Prepare a rollback brief
verbs.summary: When parity or a smoke check fails, brief the release owner on the version to switch back to, why, what changes and what to check after.
verbs.outcome: A rollback brief; the release owner decides and acts.

slots.name: release_receipt
slots.description: Pin of the failed or partial receipt.

steps: Name the rollback version from the receipt; if none was recorded, end blocked with that question.
Cite the failed checks and parity evidence, and say what users would see change.
List the checks to run after the switch back. Never switch versions yourself.

acceptance.check: The brief validates against template.rollback-brief's schema.
rollback_version equals the receipt's rollback target.
